issue.title: Support Android officially

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
Given that:
- mobile devices are becoming more and more powerful,
- the most known issues with NIO and SSLEngine in ADK were fixed since Ice Cream Sandwich, and
- users obviously want to reuse their codecs and handlers in their mobile application.

Therefore, I think it will be worthwhile to support Android officially.  However, we had to rely on manual testing and user report to know if Netty works fine on Android or not, and it was painful to both the users and the devs.

To address the mentioned problem and to support Android in a saner way:
- Write the testsuite that extends our current testsuite, which runs the testsuite in an Android emulator.
  - One of the tasks to make this possible is going to be writing a simple application that runs a series of JUnit tests and logs its output to the Android console.
- Apply sensible defaults
  - The default allocator could be unpooled heap allocator for example and we should be less memory hungry.

Unfortunately, I don't have enough time to work on this.  If there's a volunteer, I'd be happy to set up a Jenkins account for him/her so he or she can play with it.
